jobs.title: Google Ads Media Buyer
jobs.excerpt: Everyone can run a search campaign.  Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
jobs.description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

Calling all innovators - find your future at Fiserv.

We're Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants and consumers to one another millions of times a day - quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we're involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv.

As a Manager, Business Intelligence & Analytics, you will serve as a dedicated analytical leader supporting one of Fiserv's largest strategic client relationships. You will be responsible for delivering data-driven insights, executive reporting, performance analytics, and business intelligence solutions that help internal and external stakeholders make informed decisions.

You will partner closely with client stakeholders, relationship management, operations, finance, compliance, product, and technology teams to transform complex data into actionable business insights. jobs.excerpt: The Senior Staff Accountant of Accounts Payable reviews bills for coding accuracy above an established materiality threshold, serves as the final layer of review for PO-backed bills (matching bills to POs so a secondary AP reviewer is not required), and approves vendor profiles added or updated by Staff Accountants, including checking the vendor master file for duplicates.
jobs.description:
The Senior Staff Accountant of Accounts Payable reviews bills for coding accuracy above an established materiality threshold, serves as the final layer of review for PO-backed bills (matching bills to POs so a secondary AP reviewer is not required), and approves vendor profiles added or updated by Staff Accountants, including checking the vendor master file for duplicates. This role also supports inbox management, prepares AP payment runs, supports cash forecasting with Treasury, backs up the Practice Payment function of AP, and helps train and mentor Staff Accountants by reviewing errors and building processes to reduce them going forward. The ideal candidate is highly detail-oriented, prioritizes quality over speed, thinks independently, and is comfortable using AI tools (such as Claude) to improve processes.
We are flexible with respect to geographic location, and the ideal candidate will be comfortable working remotely/work from home within the US or be based from Bethesda, MD office.

Primary Duties:

  • Review bills coded by Staff Accountants for coding accuracy above an established materiality threshold, including proper treatment of prepaid vs. current expenses, amortization schedules, and service periods.
  • Serve as the final layer of review for PO-backed bills, matching bills to POs and catching missing fields the PO did not carry over (e.g., prepaid coding, amortization schedules), so a secondary AP reviewer is not required.
  • Review and approve new or updated vendor payee profiles, checking the vendor master file for duplicates and carefully distinguishing vendors from partner practices before approval.
  • Prepare AP payment runs, support cash forecasting with the Treasury team, and support or resolve vendor statement reconciliations escalated by Staff Accountants.
  • Help manage the P2P inbox, back up the Practice Payment function of AP, mentor Staff Accountants by reviewing errors and building processes to reduce them going forward, and support testing of scenarios during the Tipalti-to-Zip migration.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Able to work core East Coast business hours (company hours are 8:00 AM-5:00 PM Eastern); available no later than 10:00 AM Eastern.
  • 2-3+ years of full-time accounting experience.
  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
  • Strong accounting foundation, including solid understanding of prepaid vs. current expenses and amortization schedules.
  • Strong understanding of distinguishing operating expenses (OpEx) from cost of service (COS) expenses.
  • Highly detail-oriented; prioritizes quality and accuracy over speed.
  • Able to think independently while knowing when to escalate; comfortable serving as the final say on coding once familiar with the company's cost centers and chart of accounts.
  • Strong organizational and prioritization skills; able to manage competing priorities using a due-date-driven approach.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to handle sensitive vendor and practice communications professionally.
  • Willing and able to use AI tools (e.g., Claude) to improve processes and automation.

Preferred knowledge, skills, and/or abilities:

  • Healthcare industry experience is a plus.
  • Comfortable training and supporting more junior team members.
  • Experience administering T&E tools such as Navan or Expensify.
  • Experience in a post-PO AP environment, matching POs to bills.
  • Proficiency with spreadsheets (Excel and/or Google Sheets); comfortable working in a Google-heavy organization.
  • Prior experience training, mentoring, or reviewing the work of others

Physical Requirements:

    Primarily sedentary, remote desk-based work involving extended periods of sitting and computer/keyboard use. No unusual physical demands.

Who We Are:

Aledade PBC, a public benefit corporation, exists to empower the most transformational part of our health care landscape - independent primary care. We were founded in 2014, and since then, we've become the largest network of independent primary care in the country - helping practices, health centers and clinics deliver better care to their patients and thrive in value-based care. Additionally, by creating value-based contracts across a wide variety of health plans, we aim to flip the script on the traditional fee-for-service model. Our work strengthens continuity of care, aligns incentives and ensures primary care physicians are paid for what they do best - keeping patients healthy. If you want to help create a health care system that is good for patients, good for practices and good for society - and if you're eager to join a collaborative, inclusive and remote-first culture - you've come to the right place.

What Does This Mean for You?

At Aledade PBC, you will be part of a creative culture that is driven by a passion for tackling complex issues with respect, open-mindedness and a desire to learn. You will collaborate with team members who bring a wide range of experiences, interests, backgrounds, beliefs and achievements to their work - and who are all united by a shared passion for public health and a commitment to the Aledade mission.
In addition to time off to support work-life balance and enjoyment, we offer the following comprehensive benefits package designed for the overall well-being of our team members:
Flexible work schedules and the ability to work remotely are available for many roles
Health, dental and vision insurance paid up to 80% for employees, dependents and domestic partners
Robust time-off plan (21 days of PTO in your first year)
Two paid volunteer days and 11 paid holidays
12 weeks paid parental leave for all new parents
Six weeks paid sabbatical after six years of service
Educational Assistant Program and Clinical Employee Reimbursement Program
401(k) with up to 4% match
Stock options
And much more!
At Aledade PBC, we don’t just accept differences, we celebrate them! We strive to attract, develop and retain highly qualified individuals representing the diverse communities where we live and work. Aledade is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. Employment policies and decisions at Aledade are based on merit, qualifications, performance and business needs. All qualified candidates will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth or medical conditions related to pregnancy or childbirth), gender identity or expression, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, legally protected genetic information, marital status, veteran status, or sexual orientation.

jobs.excerpt: Front Row isn't a traditional agency.  We're a connected growth engine, combining strategy, creative, media, and Amazon performance to scale beauty, wellness, and consumer brands.
jobs.description:
Front Row isn't a traditional agency. We're a connected growth engine, combining strategy, creative, media, and Amazon performance to scale beauty, wellness, and consumer brands. Our difference is in what we connect, and the results it drives: faster growth, stronger conversion, and full-funnel efficiency across every platform.

Born from the unification of five commerce-first agencies, Front Row's Amazon Marketplace Growth division operates at the intersection of brand and performance to help emerging and established brands scale strategically on Amazon.

About Front Row Amazon Marketplace Growth

Front Row's Amazon Marketplace Growth division is purpose-built to help brands scale profitably and strategically on Amazon. We support every stage of the Amazon journey, from early-stage channel entry to enterprise-level expansion, through a connected service model that spans 3P Management, 1P Management, and 3P Distribution.

What sets us apart is our ability to match business models to business moments across a brand's Amazon lifecycle. Whether we're helping a brand take control of its presence through 3P Management, streamline vendor operations via 1P, or unlocking new revenue through our owned retail Distribution model, we operate with agility, transparency, and a relentless focus on performance.

Our team blends deep Amazon fluency with category-specific expertise across CPG, offering tailored strategies, full-funnel optimization, and executional excellence.

As part of Front Row's broader connected commerce offering, we bring Amazon into alignment with a brand's DTC, retail, and marketing ecosystem, ensuring that success on-platform fuels momentum off-platform, too.

The Role

For many brands, the biggest limit on marketplace growth sits upstream. It might be a distribution gap, a pricing conflict, weak brand awareness, or a retail plan pulling in another direction. To grow a brand on marketplaces, you have to understand the whole business.

As Enterprise Director, CPG, you'll be the connected commerce partner to Front Row's premier CPG brands. You'll support each brand's omnichannel strategy so what we learn off-channel sharpens what we do on marketplace. You'll lead Front Row's work directly and partner with the brand's other agency and retail partners where Front Row isn't running the work.

This is an analytical strategy role that requires hands-on experience leading enterprise CPG brands. You're as comfortable identifying strengths and weaknesses within a business, reading a marketing mix model, or presenting a strategic guidance plan. You'll lead strategy, own revenue growth across your portfolio, and build a team of omnichannel leaders to better guide holistic CPG growth across a complex retail system.

Your Impact at Front Row

Lead Brand Growth Strategy

  • Shape each brand's annual growth plan, turning revenue, margin, and share targets into a clear strategy and the execution to deliver it.

  • Diagnose what's holding growth back, whether it's brand awareness and demand generation, pricing and promotion, product-market fit, or retail performance, and trace how each constraint affects marketplace results.

  • Balance long-term brand building against near-term demand capture, and show how that balance affects growth, MER, and margin.

  • Define the role of each sales outlet (DTC, marketplaces, specialty and mass retail), and where growth in one lifts or cannibalizes another.

  • Apply category context specific to CPG.

  • Help brands earn visibility in AI-driven discovery through AEO/GEO, with LLM citations a core Front Row focus in the years ahead.

  • Give strategic direction to Front Row's Amazon team, who own day-to-day activation on marketplace.

Guide Decisions with Data and Modeling

  • Set the measurement agenda for each enterprise client in partnership with Front Row Analytics [and our MMM partner], and turn what works across your portfolio into Front Row's standard for enterprise brands.

  • Make MER each brand's headline efficiency measure, and use MMM to explain what drives it: each lever's contribution, saturation point, and marginal return.

  • Measure brand building as rigorously as performance, tracking awareness, consideration, and branded search demand alongside MMM's long-term effects.

  • Combine MMM, lift and geo holdout tests, and attribution into one measurement approach, and model the payoff of different spend levels in P&L terms a CFO recognizes.

  • Bring DTC, marketplace, retail POS, and SPINS or Circana data into a single MER-anchored scoreboard for brand leadership, using Front Row's proprietary tools, including Catapult, to move faster.

Own Portfolio Growth

  • Own your portfolio's revenue and growth targets, and report on both directly to Front Row leadership.

  • Expand each relationship by solving the brand's next growth problem, bringing in Front Row's strategy, creative, content, media, affiliate, and Distribution teams.

  • Build the strategy and measurement case at the center of enterprise CPG pitches, and be a visible voice for Front Row in the category.

Build the Team

  • Lead Front Row's CPG client pods, developing Client Partners and Account Directors into data-fluent strategists whose recommendations are backed by evidence.

  • Bring Front Row's strategy, analytics, creative, content, and media leads together around each brand as one connected team.

Your First Year

First 90 days: Build relationships with leadership at our top CPG partners and with your team. Assess each brand's growth levers, constraints, and measurement maturity, then deliver a growth point of view for your largest accounts with a MER target attached.

By six months: Every enterprise brand in your portfolio has a connected commerce plan tied to a total-business MER target, plus a measurement roadmap built with Front Row Analytics.

By twelve months: You've led at least one MMM-guided budget shift that improved MER and delivered incremental growth, hit your portfolio revenue targets, and expanded Front Row's role with several top partners. Your team is known across Front Row for its strategic and analytical depth.

The Experience We're Looking For

Must-haves

  • 7+ years in growth strategy, marketing strategy, or analytics, much of it leading omnichannel work for enterprise CPG brands.

  • Experience as the strategic leader on enterprise CPG brands, with a clear view of how retail, pricing, brand building, and advertising work together to drive growth.

  • Experience setting real budgets with MER targets, marketing mix models, and lift tests, and knowing which assumptions to question.

  • An analytical mind that finds the insight that matters in messy data and presents it so leadership acts.

  • Ownership of revenue targets for a client portfolio or brand P&L, with a record of growing both.

  • Experience building teams and leading other managers.

  • A bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.

Strong additions

  • Highly preferred: Hands-on AEO/GEO experience, especially earning brand citations and visibility in LLM answers.

  • Experience rebuilding a brand's measurement around MER, MMM, and brand health tracking, and moving leadership away from platform-reported ROAS.

  • Comfort pairing DTC and marketplace results with category share and retail POS data.

  • A brand-side, founder, operator, or strategy consulting chapter in your career.

  • Experience spanning prestige and mass Beauty, or specialty and mass VMS, plus an active presence in the CPG community.

How We'll Know It's Working

  • Portfolio revenue: retention and growth against annual targets, and the breadth of Front Row services each brand uses

  • Brand growth: profitable revenue and share gains across retail, DTC, and marketplaces

  • Evidence-led budgets: MER improvement and MMM-guided budget shifts that delivered incremental revenue, with every enterprise brand running a unified measurement plan

  • Brand strength: growth in awareness, consideration, and branded search demand

  • AI discovery: growth in brand citations and visibility across LLM answers

  • Team strength: stronger strategists on your team, promotions from within, and top performers who stay

Benefits

  • Health, dental, and vision

  • PTO

  • Summer Fridays

  • Wellness and commuter benefits

  • Work with a fun, consultative team of experts

  • Location – Ideally Hybrid in NYC - Open to fully remote

SALARY: $150,000 - $180,000 + Bonus

Description

MEDvidi is an AI-powered mental healthcare clinic setting a new standard for safe, effective, and scalable psychiatric care in the United States.

We combine licensed providers with proprietary AI tools to deliver consistent, outcomes-driven treatment for conditions like ADHD, anxiety, depression, and more. MEDvidi’s technology automates charting, follow-ups, and treatment planning, freeing providers to focus on patient care while improving efficiency and clinical quality.

As a Senior Product Designer on our Patient Journey team, you’ll own the patient-facing flows that turn first-time visitors into patients who start and stay in treatment. Your design decisions show up directly in our conversion and retention numbers, not just in the mockups.

You’ll be the dedicated designer for the Patient Journey squad, partnering daily with a product manager, frontend and backend engineers, QA, and a data analyst, and reporting to our Director of Product. You own patient-facing flows end to end, from early prototype through validation to a shipped, measurable result in a HIPAA-regulated, AI-first environment where both speed and clarity matter.

Responsibilities

  • Own patient-facing conversion flows end to end, from framing the problem through prototyping, validation, and shipped design.
  • Design flows that clearly communicate MEDvidi’s care model and move patients toward the next step, anticipating their real questions and objections.
  • Partner closely with product and engineering to break “too hard / too long” down into shippable tests that launch in weeks.
  • Dig into product analytics and user research yourself to tie every design decision to a concrete metric: conversion, activation, or retention.
  • Use AI tools to prototype quickly, iterate with your PM, and validate ideas against real users before anything goes to build.

This role is not for you if

  • You need a detailed brief before starting work. Requirements here are gathered by you, not handed to you, there is no PM or BA writing specs for AI Track.
  • You prefer managing people over hands-on design. This is an IC role with no direct reports; the impact comes from the quality of your own design decisions.
  • You design exclusively in Figma and hand off static specs. Prototyping at MEDvidi happens in code on the real codebase using AI agents, comfort with a code editor is a daily requirement, not a nice-to-have.

Requirements

  • Senior-level product design experience (5+ years) with a strong track record of owning user-facing B2C conversion flows.
  • Demonstrable conversion ownership: you can point to a specific flow where you owned a metric, know the before/after numbers, and can explain your own contribution versus seasonality or marketing.
  • Outcome-driven: comfortable pulling your own data (Amplitude, GA, Metabase, or similar) and running or reading research, rather than waiting for hand-offs.
  • Ownership mindset: you break engineering constraints down to the atoms, negotiate scope, and ship meaningful tests fast.
  • AI as a working tool: fluent with at least one prototyping/AI tool (Lovable, v0, Bolt, Cursor, Claude, or similar) and clear-eyed about where AI should and shouldn’t be used.
  • Fluent Russian and solid working English (B2+)

Would be a plus

  • Experience with regulated or healthcare/telehealth products (HIPAA, NIST).

What we offer

  • High-impact environment: A chance to contribute to a product-driven company in the medical tech space.
  • Growth & compensation: Clear growth opportunities and a competitive compensation package.
  • Remote-first: Fully remote long-term collaboration under a B2B model.
  • Health & wellness: Health insurance after the probation period, plus sports & wellness compensation.
  • Career development: Clear growth opportunities, including personalized English lessons via Preply.
  • Time off: 19 paid vacation days annually, 4 additional wellness days each year, and paid sick leave for the first 5 working days.
  • Culture: Thoughtful gifts for key life events and offline corporate events.

Product Manager — Virtualisation & Cloud Infrastructure

Location: Remote in Europe / EMEA

Virtuozzo is a provider of infrastructure software for AI and the cloud, helping cloud service providers, SaaS companies, and enterprises build and operate efficient, scalable infrastructure. We combine an optimized operating system with orchestration, management, automation, and protection to deliver mainframe-like efficiency, performance, reliability, versatility, and security—while reducing overall cost and complexity.

Our Virtuozzo Infrastructure System (V/IS) brings together compute, storage, and networking to support traditional applications, cloud-native workloads, and AI services. We help organisations modernise their infrastructure, make better use of their hardware, and bring new cloud- and GPU-powered services to market on their own infrastructure and under their own brand.

Our technology serves more than 100,000 companies in over 100 countries. With deep engineering roots, we pioneered container-based virtualisation and continue to contribute to foundational open-source projects, including OpenVZ, the Linux kernel, Kubernetes, CRIU, KVM, and OpenStack.

We are looking for a Product Manager for V/IS to help shape the future of the Virtuozzo product suite, including virtualisation, cloud management platforms, and infrastructure solutions for CSP, MSP, and SME markets.

jobs.title: Demand Generation Manager
jobs.excerpt: Job Summary:We are looking for a highly driven, creative, and commercially minded Demand Generation Manager who knows how to create demand, engage potential buyers, and turn prospects into qualified sales opportunities.
jobs.description:
Job Summary:

We are looking for a highly driven, creative, and commercially minded Demand Generation Manager who knows how to create demand, engage potential buyers, and turn prospects into qualified sales opportunities.

This is not a conventional email marketing role. We are looking for someone who can build and execute an integrated demand generation strategy using outbound marketing, email campaigns, marketing automation, account-based marketing, and data-driven prospecting.

You will own the demand generation engine, from identifying the right audience and developing compelling messaging to launching campaigns, nurturing prospects, generating qualified meetings, and contributing to revenue growth.

We need someone who thinks strategically but is equally comfortable getting hands-on with campaign execution, writing compelling emails, building automation workflows, researching prospects, and analyzing campaign performance.

Key Responsibilities

1. Email Marketing & Lifecycle Campaigns

  • Own the overall email marketing strategy and execution.
  • Develop targeted email campaigns for different audience segments, industries, buyer personas, and service offerings.
  • Build and manage automated email sequences, nurture workflows, newsletters, and lifecycle campaigns.
  • Create compelling email copy, subject lines, CTAs, and messaging that drive engagement and conversions.
  • Develop re-engagement campaigns for dormant leads, closed-lost opportunities, inactive contacts, and existing databases.
  • Implement audience segmentation, behavioral triggers, lead scoring, and personalized communication.
  • Continuously test and optimize email deliverability, engagement, conversion rates, and campaign performance.
  • Maintain email marketing best practices, sender reputation, domain health, and compliance.

2. Outbound Marketing & Prospecting

  • Develop and execute scalable outbound marketing strategies targeting relevant decision-makers and potential customers.
  • Build targeted prospect databases using ICPs, industry segments, company attributes, and buyer personas.
  • Design personalized cold email campaigns and multi-touch outreach sequences.
  • Develop outbound messaging strategies tailored to different industries, business challenges, and buying motivations.
  • Execute coordinated outreach campaigns across email, LinkedIn, and other relevant channels.
  • Identify opportunities to engage high-value accounts through personalized and relevant outreach.
  • Experiment with different outreach approaches, messaging angles, offers, and sequences.
  • Establish processes for prospect research, contact enrichment, list validation, and campaign execution.
  • Work closely with Sales to convert positive responses into qualified meetings and opportunities.

3. Demand Generation Strategy & Campaign Development

  • Develop and execute integrated demand generation strategies aligned with business and revenue objectives.
  • Build campaigns that generate awareness, capture existing demand, nurture prospects, and create new buying opportunities.
  • Develop industry-specific and persona-based campaigns with tailored messaging and value propositions.
  • Identify new opportunities to reach potential customers through targeted campaigns, partnerships, databases, and outbound channels.
  • Plan and execute account-based marketing (ABM) campaigns for high-value target accounts.
  • Develop campaign calendars, messaging frameworks, content requirements, and distribution strategies.
  • Collaborate with Product Marketing and Content teams to translate positioning, customer insights, and value propositions into demand generation campaigns.
  • Identify opportunities to reactivate existing leads and accelerate prospects through the sales funnel.

4. Marketing Automation & CRM Management

  • Own demand generation workflows and campaign automation within HubSpot.
  • Build automated nurture sequences based on audience behavior, engagement, lifecycle stages, and lead qualification.
  • Implement lead scoring, segmentation, routing, and qualification workflows.
  • Maintain CRM data quality, campaign tracking, attribution, and contact lifecycle management.
  • Integrate prospecting and outreach platforms with CRM systems to maintain a connected acquisition workflow.
  • Develop reporting dashboards to measure campaign performance, lead progression, and pipeline contribution.
  • Continuously identify opportunities to improve marketing automation and operational efficiency.

5. Data, Analytics & Performance Optimization

  • Track and analyze campaign performance across email, outbound, nurture, and ABM initiatives.
  • Monitor positive reply rates, qualified meetings, MQLs, SQLs, opportunities, and marketing-sourced pipeline.
  • Measure email engagement, deliverability, bounce rates, unsubscribes, and conversion performance.
  • Analyze campaign performance by industry, audience, messaging, channel, and buyer persona.
  • Conduct A/B testing across email copy, subject lines, CTAs, offers, and outreach sequences.
  • Identify underperforming campaigns and develop actionable optimization strategies.
  • Present regular performance reports, insights, experiments, and recommendations to marketing leadership.
  • Connect demand generation activities to actual business outcomes and revenue contribution.

6. Sales Alignment & Pipeline Development

  • Work closely with Sales to align campaign strategies with sales priorities and revenue targets.
  • Develop clear qualification criteria and processes for handing over sales-ready leads.
  • Collaborate on outbound messaging, target account lists, and industry-specific sales plays.
  • Monitor lead-to-meeting, meeting-to-opportunity, and opportunity-to-customer conversion rates.
  • Gather feedback from Sales to improve targeting, messaging, and lead quality.
  • Build campaigns that support the entire customer acquisition journey, from initial engagement to closed-won opportunities.

Tools & Technology

Hands-on experience with several of the following platforms is expected:

  • CRM & Marketing Automation: HubSpot, ActiveCampaign, Marketo.
  • Prospecting & Data Intelligence: Apollo.io, Clay, ZoomInfo, Lusha.
  • Cold Email & Outreach: Instantly, Smartlead, Lemlist, Salesloft, Outreach.
  • Email Platforms: HubSpot Marketing Hub, Mailchimp, Brevo.
  • Analytics & Reporting: Google Analytics 4, Looker Studio, HubSpot Reporting.
  • LinkedIn Prospecting: LinkedIn Sales Navigator.

You do not need to have used every platform, but you must understand how to build and manage an effective demand generation technology stack.

Requirements

  • 4-6 years of experience in B2B demand generation, email marketing, outbound marketing, or growth marketing.
  • Demonstrated experience building and executing email marketing and outbound acquisition campaigns.
  • Strong understanding of B2B buyer journeys, ICP development, audience segmentation, and lead qualification.
  • Proven ability to develop effective cold email campaigns and personalized outreach sequences.
  • Hands-on experience with marketing automation platforms, preferably HubSpot.
  • Experience with prospecting, contact enrichment, and outbound campaign tools.
  • Excellent email copywriting and communication skills.
  • Strong understanding of email deliverability, sender reputation, domain warm-up, and email authentication protocols (SPF, DKIM, DMARC).
  • Experience developing nurture journeys, lead scoring, and CRM workflows.
  • Understanding of account-based marketing and multi-channel outreach.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to translate campaign data into actionable improvements.
  • Ability to manage multiple campaigns independently while maintaining strategic direction and execution quality.

What Will Make You Stand Out

  • You have built an outbound engine from scratch and can demonstrate its contribution to qualified pipeline.
  • You understand how to combine personalization, automation, and scale without compromising outreach quality.
  • You know how to write emails that generate meaningful responses rather than generic promotional messages.
  • You understand the difference between lead generation and demand generation.
  • You can identify the right audiences, find decision-makers, and develop campaigns around their actual business challenges.
  • You have successfully executed ABM and industry-specific demand generation campaigns.
  • You understand how to reactivate dormant databases and turn existing contacts into new opportunities.
  • You are comfortable experimenting with AI-powered prospect research, personalization, enrichment, and campaign automation.
  • You think in terms of meetings, opportunities, pipeline, and revenue rather than email volume and open rates.

Who We Are Looking For

We want a demand creator, not an email operator.

Someone who is curious about buyer psychology, understands how businesses make purchasing decisions, knows how to initiate meaningful conversations, and can turn a database into a revenue-generating asset.

Someone who can think strategically, write exceptionally well, execute independently, experiment continuously, and take full ownership of outcomes.

If you believe demand generation is about sending thousands of emails, generating contact lists, and reporting open rates, this role is not for you.

If you know how to identify the right buyers, reach them with the right message, create interest, and turn that interest into qualified business opportunities, we want to hear from you.

We are partnering with an innovative data center development and infrastructure company supporting the rapidly growing AI and high-performance computing (HPC) industry.

The company develops and operates specialized data center facilities for GPU cloud providers, AI infrastructure companies, and enterprise customers. Its projects range from smaller multi-megawatt deployments to large-scale facilities exceeding 30 MW, including the conversion of existing industrial buildings into high-density computing environments.

We are seeking a Senior Data Center Engineer to oversee critical infrastructure projects from initial site evaluation and utility coordination through engineering design, construction, commissioning, and operational handoff.

This is an owner-side engineering opportunity for someone who can take technical ownership of infrastructure workstreams, coordinate across utilities and external engineering partners, and help deliver reliable, high-density AI data center environments.

  • Site Evaluation & Infrastructure Planning: Evaluate potential sites for electrical power availability, utility capacity, fiber connectivity, water access, structural requirements, and permitting constraints. Develop phased capacity plans, cost estimates, and implementation schedules.

  • Mechanical & Cooling Systems: Review mechanical infrastructure designs for high-density GPU deployments, including air cooling, direct-to-chip liquid cooling, coolant distribution units (CDUs), and facility water systems. Evaluate redundancy, scalability, cost, and implementation timelines.

- Professional Engineer (PE) license.

jobs.description:
Director, AP Italian Language and Culture, Curriculum and Assessment

College Board – AP & I

Location: This is a remote role. Candidates who live near CB offices have the option of being fully remote or hybrid (Tuesday and Wednesday in office). All CB employees are required to occasionally travel to meet in person for business purposes.

Role Type:This is a full-time position


About the Team

The AP Curriculum and Assessment Team at College Board (125+ staff) collaborates with colleagues across all aspects of the AP Program to develop, manage, and deliver AP’s 43 courses in a wide variety of subject areas. AP® is a rigorous academic program built on the commitment, passion, and hard work of students and educators from secondary schools and higher education. AP provides willing and academically prepared high school students with the opportunity to study and learn at the college level. AP’s course teams comprised of educators and disciplinary experts ensure that course curricula are aligned to higher education expectations and reflect the state of the art in the discipline, contribute to instructional resources and tools for teachers, and develop assessments that allow students in these courses to demonstrate their mastery of course content and skills. AP leads in strategic use of AI to expand student access, strengthen instructional design and professional support, and enhance assessment creation and exam analysis. The English, World Languages, and Arts department, which includes English Literature, English Language, Spanish Language, Italian Language, French Language, German Language, Italian Language, Japanese Language, Latin, Music Theory, Spanish Literature, and Art and Design is currently comprised of approximately 35 people supporting 14 courses in the AP portfolio. 


About the Opportunity

As the Director I, AP Italian Language and Culture you will be responsible for preserving and improving the quality and validity of the AP Program’s core deliverables within the subject domain: the exam, the course curriculum, and the professional development content. You are also responsible for item development and management from authoring to administration; training and collaborating with subject-matter experts (SMEs), typically college professors and secondary school teachers. You will ethically and effectively integrate AI technologies in assessment creation and review. This includes judiciously using AI assisted tools to support fairness, validity, and innovation in AP assessments. You will train SMEs on assessment development protocols, translate between academics and technical experts (psychometricians), and collaborate to develop formative assessment materials and resources to support AP Italian Language and Culture teachers worldwide. You will serve as a point of contact in AP for committees and communities of subject-matter experts and will be responsible for the curriculum and assessment for AP Italian Language and Culture, and, in partnership with other AP teams, further the strategic growth of AP Italian Language and Culture across the globe. Additionally, you may have the opportunity to present, speak, and moderate dialogue with academic and membership audiences to ensure that ongoing change and improvement within AP courses and exams is understood, accepted, and supported in secondary and post-secondary educational communities.  


In this role, you will:


Assessment Development and Scoring (45-75%)  

  • Serve as an assessment leader for AP Italian Language and Culture, with primary responsibility for assessment development for AP Italian Language and Culture. Your work in developing and revising test content is of the quality that requires only minimal adjustments based on feedback from your manager and other program leaders. 
  • Independently lead processes for authoring and revising assessment content, including training educator constituents and leveraging generative AI to author and/or review assessment content, improving and/or making more efficient assessment processes and outputs.
  • Independently lead the development and management of assessment content (formative and summative) and scoring materials for AP Italian Language and Culture through iterative review stages with multiple internal and external stakeholders, including the AP Italian Language and Culture Team, Assessment Production team, Test Development Committee, and the Chief Reader, as appropriate.
  • Independently lead the development of assessment forms for AP Italian Language and Culture, ensuring the AP Exam development aligns with approved curricula and test specifications.
  • Lead multiple face-to-face, weekend meetings, and virtual meetings (during work week, evenings, or weekends) annually with the AP Italian Language and Culture Test Development Committee. You strategize and develop an agenda and approach to ensure the committee’s meeting time is of the highest productivity; you successfully adapt and pivot during the meeting as needed; and you successfully resolve all post-meeting item content edits.
  • Train and directly supervise Test Development Committee members in AP Italian Language and Culture as content development contributors and reviewers. Recruit educators for the AP Italian Language and Culture Development Committee and other opportunities to support AP Program.
  • Lead the successful scoring of student responses for AP Italian Language and Culture Exams at the annual scoring event in person and online—the “AP Reading”—and produce AP Reading publications materials for teacher and student use. You plan all year, with increasing intensity in the months leading up to the Reading, ensuring all workflow steps for this incredibly complex event, as well as all post-Reading activities, are accounted for and successfully executed. 

Assessment Quality and Process (10-15%) 

  • Contribute to current research and best practices in assessment, and engage regularly with AP Curriculum & Assessment colleagues to align on standards and shared principles guiding AP’s assessment directions 
  • Support assessment workstreams within the AP English, World Languages, and Arts Department. 
  • Contribute to processes for efficient, high-quality assessment development. 
  • Contribute to initiatives to refine and improve question task models as well as exam design in collaboration with AP Curriculum & Assessment leaders and aligned to other College Board initiatives to achieve psychometric and disciplinary best practices on AP Italian Language and Culture exams. 
  • Monitor exam validity, security, reliability, fairness, and quality, as well as reader reliability in accordance with established Program thresholds for AP Italian Language and Culture exam, identifying areas for improvement and executing on targeted improvement initiatives. 
  • Collaborate with psychometrics and AP Curriculum & Assessment staff to establish fair, reliable, and valid cut scores for AP Italian Language and Culture exam. 

 

Course Development, Program Support, and Stakeholder Engagement (5-25%)

  • Refine and improve AP Italian Language and Culture Framework to ensure clear and explicit learning outcomes that align with strategic priorities, including ensuring college/disciplinary standards as well as expanding the scope of reaching a broader audience of AP students.  
  • Collaborate with AP teams to support the development of new products for AP Italian Language and Culture designed to address unmet teacher instructional needs, potentially including developing prototypes, participating in small-scale market-testing, and creating models for subsequent development in conjunction with other AP workstreams.  
  • Recruit educators for the AP Italian Language and Culture Development Committee and other opportunities to support AP Program. 
  • Serve as a recognized and trusted resource within the educator community by collaboration and engagement with the community to drive teacher satisfaction with AP Italian Language and Culture and its exam. 
  • Collaborate with the AP Professional learning team to support AP Italian Language and Culture consultants and teachers. 
  • Work with the AP Higher Education team to co-develop and implement plans to raise college and university awareness of AP Italian Language and Culture courses and exams, including recruiting college faculty to participate in the AP Reading, co-leading the planning and execution of discipline-specific AP Faculty Colloquia events, and supporting Visiting and Virtual Fellows Programs.  

About You

To qualify for this role, you must have:

  • A Master’s degree in Italian Language or a directly related discipline, and knowledge of current trends in the discipline (required), although a doctorate in the discipline is strongly preferred  
  • Native to near-native fluency in Italian.
  • Expertise in Italian Language with at least 5 years of experience in standardized assessment development or related work; experience with digital assessment and teaching preferred 
  • Strong oral and written communication skills, with solid technical proficiency and a customer-focused mindset 
  • Excellent organizational and planning skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and maintain close attention to detail, including proofreading 
  • Demonstrated ability to implement processes and procedures, manage project plans and schedules, and maintain tracking documentation 
  • Strong interpersonal and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across all levels, and engage in giving and receiving constructive feedback 
  • Ability to travel 6-8 times per year, plus up to two additional weeks for the AP Reading; must be eligible to work in the United States 

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and comfort with learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively.
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success
  • Authorization to work in the United States

About Our Process

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise such as live coding, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than a paycheck: we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.


A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

  • The hiring range for this role is $96,000 - $135,000.
  • Your exact salary will depend on your location, experience, and how your background compares to others in similar roles at the College Board.
  • We aim to make our best offer upfront, rooted in fairness, transparency, and market data.
  • We adjust salaries by location to ensure fairness, no matter where you live.

You’ll have open, transparent conversations about compensation, benefits, and what it’s like to work at College Board throughout your hiring process. Check out our careers page for more.

jobs.excerpt: Who We AreGreat Minds is a high-growth, mission-driven organization founded by educators in 2007.
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Great Minds is a high-growth, mission-driven organization founded by educators in 2007. As a for-profit, Public Benefit Corporation, we believe all students deserve access to meaningful, challenging content—and all teachers deserve tools that are intuitive, effective, and built for the realities of today’s classrooms.

We develop high-quality, knowledge-rich math, science and ELA curricula grounded in research and designed in collaboration with educators. Our materials reflect real classroom needs and are built to drive lasting student outcomes.

We are committed to usability, coherence, and practical implementation—supporting teachers not just through curriculum, but with professional learning, purposeful technology, and responsive service that enable strong adoption and impact.

What We Build

Our products—Eureka Math and Eureka Math², Wit & Wisdom, Geodes, and the newly launched Arts & Letters ELA—are trusted by thousands of schools and districts nationwide.

  • Eureka Math is the most widely used math curriculum in the U.S., and is focused on balancing conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, and application.

  • Wit & Wisdom® and Arts & Letters ELA™ anchor our reading strategy with content-rich, grade-level instruction that integrates literature, history, and the arts, grounded in the science of reading. Geodes® complements our reading suite with decodable texts that pair phonics with meaningful content to support early literacy.

These programs reflect a shared belief in high expectations, joyful rigor, and deep respect for educators and students.

Where We’re Headed

Great Minds is entering a new stage of growth and product maturity. We are focused on building more connected, customer-informed experiences across the full educator journey—from curriculum to professional learning to platform and support.

Our long-term vision is to become a true partner in impact—not just delivering curriculum, but supporting educators in achieving outcomes at scale.


Job Purpose

Reporting to the Associate Director, Print Operations, the Senior Print Procurement Analyst owns strategic sourcing and procurement for Great Minds’ print manufacturing portfolio, one of the organization’s largest categories of annual spend. This role leads competitive sourcing events, builds the cost models that drive award decisions, negotiates pricing and terms with national commercial printers, and manages ongoing vendor performance to protect cost, quality, and delivery for curriculum products shipped to schools and districts nationwide.

The Senior Analyst works as a direct partner to Demand Planning, which sets title, quantity, and timing needs, and aligns with Finance, Product, and Sales to confirm annual print requirements. The role is expected to lead by example in applying AI-enabled tools to procurement: generating RFQs, normalizing and comparing supplier bids, building cost scenarios, automating purchase order workflows, and continuously improving how Great Minds buys print.


Responsibilities

Strategic Sourcing and Vendor Negotiation

  • Lead competitive sourcing events end to end: define requirements and specifications, issue RFQs/RFPs, evaluate supplier responses, and present award recommendations to Operations leadership.

  • Negotiate pricing, payment terms, capacity commitments, service levels, and multi-year agreements with national printers such as Quad/Graphics, Command Web Offset, and other commercial and specialty print manufacturers.

  • Develop and execute a category sourcing strategy for print, including vendor consolidation, capacity allocation across vendors, and qualification of new suppliers to reduce risk and cost.

  • Own measurable savings and cost-avoidance targets for print spend; track and report results to the supply chain leadership team.

  • Conduct cost analyses that account for unit price, paper, freight and landed cost, make-ready and run-length economics, inventory carrying cost, and risk.

  • Monitor paper and commodity market trends and advise leadership on timing, pricing exposure, and procurement strategy.

Analytics, Modeling, and Reporting

  • Build and maintain print cost models that interpolate vendor quotes by page count, quantity, and specification to support budgeting, reprint decisions, and what-if scenarios.

  • Develop vendor scorecards and performance analytics covering price, on-time delivery, quality, responsiveness, and capacity, and lead periodic vendor business reviews.

  • Plan, track, and report print spend, savings, and procurement metrics to the supply chain team; identify trends and recommend corrective action.

  • Support annual print budgeting and forecasting with Finance and Demand Planning, including variance analysis against plan.

AI-Enabled Procurement and Process Improvement

  • Apply AI tools (such as Claude) to generate RFQ documentation, analyze and compare supplier proposals, draft vendor communications, and streamline purchase order issuance, tracking, and reconciliation.

  • Identify, design, and implement automation and AI-driven improvements across print procurement; partner with Operations and Technology teams on tooling and workflow design.

  • Actively test, refine, train others on, and document AI-powered sourcing and procurement workflows so they become repeatable team practices.

  • Maintain key documentation, including SOPs, detailed ISBN print specifications, and vendor print status tracking.

Print Production and Vendor Management

  • Apply deep knowledge of print production (paper stock, binding, color, file formats, press requirements) to validate specifications and evaluate vendor capabilities and proposed alternatives.

  • Coordinate print schedules and vendor timelines with Demand Planning and production partners; proactively identify and escalate risks from capacity constraints, paper availability, or specification changes.

  • Manage purchase order creation, approval, and reconciliation in NetSuite in coordination with Finance, resolving invoice and pricing discrepancies with vendors.

  • Visit key vendors periodically to deepen relationships and knowledge of print manufacturing, and conduct vendor qualification and onboarding activities.

  • Collaborate with Operations leadership to align procurement strategy, supplier relationships, and policies across categories.

Requirements

Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in print procurement, print sourcing, print manufacturing, or print operations, including direct vendor negotiation with commercial printers.

  • Demonstrated experience leading large, competitive RFQ/RFP processes and making data-driven award recommendations.

  • Strong analytical skills: advanced Excel (pivot tables, lookups, modeling) and the ability to build cost comparisons, and what-if scenarios from supplier proposals.

  • Working knowledge of print production specifications and processes (offset, digital, binding and finishing, paper) sufficient to verify vendor assumptions.

  • Hands-on experience with, or demonstrated aptitude and enthusiasm for, applying AI tools to sourcing, procurement, or operational workflows.

  • Experience managing purchase orders and procurement transactions in an ERP system (NetSuite or similar).

  • Strong negotiation, vendor management, communication, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders.

  • Highly results-oriented, with personal accountability, urgency, and persistence in completing high-quality work.

  • Ability to manage multiple sourcing events and projects simultaneously without missing critical deadlines, and to anticipate roadblocks with proactive solutions.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, Smartsheet or similar project management software, and SharePoint or similar collaboration platforms.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in educational publishing, curriculum development, or K–12 education.

  • Knowledge of instructional materials manufacturing, warehousing, and distribution, including landed cost and freight considerations.

  • Experience with AI-assisted sourcing, procurement analytics, or workflow automation platforms.

  • Experience with paper purchasing.

  • Working knowledge of NetSuite and Salesforce.

Required Education

Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, business, operations, information systems, or a related field.

Status

Full-time

Location

Remote

As a growing value-based care organization, WellBe offers opportunities to gain broad exposure to the financial and operational drivers of full-risk Medicare Advantage arrangements.

Within our Global Infrastructure Business, we are seeking a highly technical and commercially savvy Sales Engineer to be a key driver of our growth strategy. This role will directly support Alpha Compute's sales organization, partnering closely with our Account Executives and Strategic Sales leadership to identify, architect, and capture new business opportunities within the AI hardware infrastructure space.

About the role

As a Sales Engineer, you are the technical linchpin supporting the broader sales organization. You will bridge the gap between complex AI hardware capabilities and our customers' business objectives. The ideal candidate possesses a deep understanding of the AI compute lifecycle, strong industry relationships, and the technical aptitude to effectively communicate the value of our high-density GPUaaS solutions to both engineering leaders and procurement officers.

You will translate complex client workloads (AI training and inference) into precise infrastructure configurations, proving that Alpha Compute's offerings provide the highest performance, reliability, and cost-efficiency in the market.

Map customer AI workloads to precise hardware configurations (e.g., NVIDIA H100/B200 clusters, InfiniBand networking).
  • Sales Organization Support: Act as the primary technical resource for Account Executives and the VP of Strategic Sales during client engagements, ensuring the sales team has the architectural backing needed to close complex deals.
  • BOM Review & Validation: Meticulously review and validate complex Bill of Materials (BOMs) provided by hardware OEMs and compute brokers to ensure 100% technical accuracy, component compatibility, and alignment with client infrastructure requirements.
  • Strategic Business Development: Partner with the sales team to identify, qualify, and secure new business opportunities with direct customers, brokers, and tier-one/two suppliers. Generate unique value propositions tailored to target companies and OEMs.
  • Cost-Benefit & TCO Analysis: Research, model, and present detailed reports showing potential customers the financial cost-benefits and ROI of utilizing Alpha Compute’s GPUaaS versus alternative cloud or on-premise deployments.
  • Proposal & RFP Development: Act as the technical lead in the development of compelling proposals, bids, and technical responses to complex Requests for Information (RFIs) and Requests for Proposals (RFPs).
  • Relationship Management: Cultivate and maintain strong, long-lasting relationships with key stakeholders, specifically focusing on customer engineering leads, technical brokers, and OEM partners.

jobs.description:
Description

Centralized monitoring is an integral part of risk-based monitoring strategy, defined as the timely, remote review of accumulating subject and operational data to help distinguish between reliable and unreliable data, trends, outliers and unusual variability using analytics and statistical methods.

The Principal Central Monitor is responsible for leading the development of new tools, instruction guidelines and analyses essential for centralized statistical review of study data from study start through to study database lock. The Principal Central Monitor enables proactive identification, communication, escalation and management of risks at the study/country/site level.

More specifically, the Principal Central Monitor must:

  • Lead effort on the development of new tools, instruction guidelines and analyses within the area of specialty, including complex and collaborative approaches with other functions.
  • Lead the development and setup of study-specific tools, analyses, and centralized monitoring plans, ensuring that the monitoring approach is aligned with study risks, critical data, and critical processes.
  • Act as the strategic and technical lead for centralized monitoring across multiple studies and for function-wide initiatives, providing direction on complex analyses, resolving escalated issues, and establishing consistent approaches and standards.
  • Assist in creating tools, techniques and processes for automating risk-based monitoring tasks (data integration automation, data retrieval automation, data mapping automation, and automated report generation).
  • Act as mentor as well as train new team members and junior staff.
  • Identify data quality trends indicative of systematic errors and potential performance issues at study/country/site level and track evidence of issues and potential risks with support from senior team members.
  • Represent centralized monitoring in cross-functional study risk assessment meetings and provide expert guidance on identification, evaluation, prioritization, mitigation, and ongoing review of study risks.
  • Provide input to leadership as needed to support development of risk characterization and reporting.

Employees may be assigned to other responsibilities that do not pertain to their former description, if they have the required experience, are qualified and/or have received adequate training.

Requirements

Education

  • ​​Bachelor’s degree in a field relevant to clinical research.

Experience

  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in central statistical monitoring with an overall 10 years of experience in two or more operational areas such as clinical monitoring, data management, drug safety, medical monitoring, biometrics, or project management.
  • Excellent understanding of statistical monitoring and Risk Based Quality Management (RBQM) and their impact on data integrity.
  • Thorough understanding of the processes associated with clinical study management, data management, and regulatory operations.
  • Knowledge of clinical trial database systems (EDC, IRT, CTMS etc.).
  • Excellent computer skills, with advanced knowledge of MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and the ability to learn and use interactive computer systems and tools.
  • Advanced level of understanding of descriptive analysis e.g. means, medians, significance, confidence intervals.
  • Demonstrated expertise in analyzing and reviewing clinical data, ability to extract pertinent information from standard study documentation, such as protocols, electronic study data systems with the ability to learn to identify trending of site/study data.
  • Must be able to work in non-traditional work environments.
  • Fluent in English (excellent oral and written).
  • Must be able to communicate clearly and effectively at all levels within the organization and with external customers.
  • Must be a fast learner and able to understand new concepts quickly.
  • Prioritization skills with ability to plan, monitor and manage workload fluidly in response to changing project demands.
  • Good understanding of project protocol, project documentation including centralized monitoring and risk-based monitoring.
  • Broad working knowledge of the roles, functions and process of conducting clinical trials.
  • Must be able to manage time effectively, working with multiple functions and requirements.
  • Must have been involved in the use of trial management or data management systems

Our company

The work environment

At Indero, you will work with brilliant and driven colleagues. Our values are collaboration, innovation, reliability and responsiveness. We offer a stimulating work environment and attractive advancement opportunities.

In this position, you will be eligible for the following perks:

  • Flexible work schedule
  • Permanent full-time position

A Global Clinical Leader In Dermatology!

Formerly known as Innovaderm, Indero is a world-renowned expert and clinical research leader in dermatology. We have more than two decades of experience serving a broad range of indications, patient populations, administration routes, and drug classes, and a global footprint.

Indero is a dual-focus CRO for dermatology and rheumatology, with 25+ years’ experience in clinical research and trial delivery. With capabilities in North America, Europe, Asia Pacific and Latin America; vast, continuously growing relationships with investigators and patients; and a dedicated research clinic through which we design and execute our own studies, Indero is the ideal CRO partner for clinical needs at global scale.

jobs.title: Google Ads Media Buyer / Growth Strategist
jobs.excerpt: Everyone can run a search campaign.  Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.
jobs.description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.
