jobs.excerpt: Please know that this is an Expression of Interest.
jobs.description:
Please know that this is an Expression of Interest. We treat EOIs differently than typical job ads. They're a less involved way for us to see who is interested in a position.

  • The default is you will not hear from us. We may not review all applications, and we will only contact people whose background fits our needs.
  • We're not able to reply to questions about this posting or about the status of your submission.

Researcher at The Future of Life Foundation

About FLF

The Future of Life Foundation (FLF) is distinct but affiliated with the Future of Life Institute. Our shared mission is to steer transformative technology towards benefiting life and away from extreme large-scale risks.

FLF focuses primarily on identifying gaps or relatively neglected efforts to fulfilling this mission, and marshalling resources to fill those gaps. To date this has involved establishing new organisations, generating new teams within established organisations, incubating fellows or nascent projects, and communicating our visions more widely in publications and workshops.

We expect our most significant focus to remain on the risks posed by transformative AI, and governance mechanisms needed to ensure that AI is beneficial to humanity. Other areas of work could include biosecurity, nuclear technology, other risks to humanity’s existence or fulfillment of its potential, and the development of tools, institutions, and communities that support these efforts.

A major (but not exclusive) focus so far has been AI tools for collective human agency: taking advantage of (and steering) new prospects from AI building blocks to differentially enable human societal decision-making during this crucial period. You can see more of our thinking on our website.

About the Role

To maintain and improve these activities, FLF needs situational awareness, insight, and generative vision: this is where researchers come in. In short, researchers work on sourcing and developing ambitious ideas to build a flourishing future, grounded in realistic scenarios for AI and other technological development. Together with the team, researchers apply their expertise, capacity for insight, network and skills to shaping these projects and nascent organisations into their best form.

You’ll be joining a team ‘in motion’, with some tentative worldview and strategy ‘bets’ already in play, but we remain open to the possibility that further strategy research updates or expands these. We want open-minded researchers who are happy to be challenged and to challenge in turn.

Besides high-level worldview and strategy, several roadmaps in motion and yet to be developed will benefit from insight and exceptional critique. Your work will often involve uncovering the best versions of a prospect as well as highlighting challenges or essential desiderata and considerations that we haven’t mapped out yet.

Researchers generally benefit from excellent generalist thinking, but there are several areas of specialisation which we anticipate being especially valuable:

  • AI safety (technical, governance, strategy)

  • AI generally (LMs and beyond) and enterprise-scale software

  • Political science, human (social) behaviour

  • Systems theory, cybernetics, and systems safety

  • Economics, especially macroeconomics of automation and labour displacement

  • Law, especially corporate law, contracting, liability, and tort law

Activities

The following are primary responsibilities of the research function at FLF: any researcher will be working or co-working on these activities with a majority of their time. Where noted, ‘wider team support’ refers to crossover activities shared with other functions, especially likely to be cross-function collaborative. These run roughly in lifecycle order, from noticing what matters, to designing an intervention, to helping launch and shape it. Researchers stay involved across that arc.

Foresight and worldview

  • Maintain and improve FLF’s situational awareness and scenario foresight, especially regarding AI and its interactions with technology and society

  • Notice and surface potentially impactful trends or scenarios; articulate important ‘arenas’ for FLF to pay attention to

  • Collaborate with partners and contacts outside of FLF on priorities and potential collaborations

Envisioning and design

  • Anticipate a) civilisational vulnerabilities and disruptions and b) opportunities for positive civilisational change, especially regarding AI

  • Collect seed ideas/visions (or innovate afresh) for types of intervention to progress toward positive change on vulnerabilities or opportunities

  • Investigate early visions for feasibility, core challenges, and downside risks

  • (With wider team support) research existing or prior related efforts and synthesise learnings, considering what might have changed, or what new insight or advantage FLF has (or could have)

  • (With wider team support) develop (socio)technological designs and roadmaps for tech, institutions, organisations, or initiatives bringing FLF’s ambitions into fruition

  • Estimate relative promise of proposals at varying stages of readiness: from early gestures to more defined roadmaps

Organization Formation, Advising, and Award Review

  • Work alongside FLF’s project development staff and founders to take promising roadmaps from concept to launch: sharpening the thesis, defining early milestones, and shaping the initial team and strategy

  • Act as a research advisor to nascent projects and organisations as they form, bringing domain expertise, critique, and connections

  • Evaluate projects in motion: surface where they are drifting from their theory of change or missing key considerations, and inform decisions to continue, expand, or redirect

Outward communication

  • (With wider team support) deliver workshops, presentations, and reports to share vision and roadmaps with partners or publicly

  • Contribute to recruitment pipeline for promising roadmaps: direct search, RFPs, job descriptions, reviewing, interviewing

  • Interact with existing or prospective fellows/founders to inspire, brainstorm, refine etc.

Tooling

  • (With wider team support) contribute to tooling, especially AI workflows, to support and compound all of the above activities

Likely Qualifications

  • Demonstrated willingness and ability to seriously consider a range of scenarios and risks from AI

  • Proven ability to perform high-quality research, preferably in AI, existential risk, or a relevant domain (political science, systems safety, economics, law, …)

  • Strong analytical, critical-thinking, communication, and problem-solving skills

  • Passion for helping to further AI safety

Additional Possible Qualifications

  • Penchant for high-quality writing (informative, understandable, appealing/approachable); perhaps an existing relevant platform or network

  • Familiarity with government and/or national security and adjacent thinktanks or suppliers

  • Experience developing and distributing software and AI applications

  • Experience with the founding of new organizations

  • Significant research achievement demonstrated by publications in top-tier conferences and journals coupled with years of pertinent academic experience

  • A track-record of impactful grantmaking

  • History of performing technical research beyond AI safety

  • A particularly strong technical background

Logistics

You will be an employee of the Future of Life Foundation, or our affiliated organization, the Future of Life Institute. Each are 501(c)(3) research non-profits.

  • Compensation and Benefits: Compensation is competitive with Bay Area tech roles (excluding equity), plus full benefits.

  • Location: The team is currently geographically distributed through North America and Western Europe, and we can welcome applicants from a wide range of locations. We should be able to sponsor US visas (without going through the visa lottery) for those who need them. We meet in person several times per year in varied locations.

Miscellaneous

If this posting is live, the role is still open. Timelines are short and we’d like to make this hire ASAP.

We are committed to diversity and equal opportunity in all aspects of our hiring process. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We welcome and encourage all qualified candidates to apply for our open positions.

  • Drive source linking across our registry backbone and supplementary sources (such as S&P Capital IQ, GLEIF, and SAM), and help define a systematic approach to resolving conflicts between sources.
  • Define and monitor quality dimensions (completeness, freshness, accuracy), and help build the automated quality gates that don't exist today.
  • Prioritize quality effort toward the subset of entities customers actually interact with most.

Cross-Functional Insight & Opportunity-Finding

  • Partner with the Director of Data Engineering and the data and ETL engineers to translate quality findings into technical fixes and prioritized work.
  • Work with Product and other cross-functional teams to share data insights and help identify new opportunities in the data, beyond quality alone.
  • Build and maintain dashboards and reports that give visibility into data health across the platform.
  • Bring a customer's-eye view to quality prioritization and to product improvements like TrustIQ, informed by direct experience with how customers actually use the data.

What You Will Need to Succeed

  • Strong SQL and BigQuery (or equivalent) data-analysis skills, with hands-on data-quality and profiling experience across multiple external data sources.
  • Comfortable working across both data warehouse and data lake environments (Snowflake), with hands-on experience using analysis and dashboarding tools built on top of them (such as Looker, Tableau, or Mode) to surface and communicate findings.
  • Familiarity with dbt or similar transformation tools is an asset, not a requirement.
  • Customer-facing or implementation background that supports quality prioritization from a user's perspective.
  • Comfort partnering across engineering, product, and other cross-functional teams to share findings and influence priorities.

Nice to Have

  • Direct experience with legal-entity or supplier data sources (OpenCorporates, S&P Capital IQ, GLEIF, SAM, or similar registries).
  • Working knowledge of master data management and entity/source-linking challenges (tax IDs, DUNS, name and address matching).
  • Experience building or defining automated data-quality gates or monitoring.

Where You Fit In

You'll sit within Data Enablement, working closely with the Director of Data Engineering, Data Architect and the data and ETL engineers on technical execution, and with Product and other cross-functional teams on sharing insights and finding new opportunities in the data. For now, you'll report directly to the CTO while Data Enablement's leadership structure is built out.

Job Title: Sales Closer (Healthcare)

Position type: Part-Time (with full-time opportunity)

Work hours: 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM Pacific Time

Work days: Monday to Friday

Salary: $6 - $7 per hour

Job code: CP-BH

Workplace: Remote

Preferred Candidate Location: Philippines

Our client, a U.S.-based medical aesthetics practice, is looking for a Sales Closer to drive patient engagement, convert inquiries into booked appointments, reactivate inactive leads, and close treatment package sales.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who thrives in sales, enjoys building relationships, and is motivated by measurable results. You'll play a key role in growing the practice by connecting with prospective and existing patients, following up on sales opportunities, and creating a welcoming, professional experience.

The ideal candidate is a proven sales closer with strong appointment-setting skills, a warm and confident phone presence, and the persistence to turn leads into paying customers.

Experience in medical spas, aesthetics, or healthcare is highly preferred, but strong sales professionals from other industries are welcome to apply. Spanish fluency is also highly preferred but not required.

The position starts at 20 hours per week, with the goal of transitioning to full-time as the practice grows. You'll receive direct training, sales scripts, and guidance to help you succeed.

Key Responsibilities

1. Lead Follow-Up, Appointment Conversion & Sales Closing (Top Priority)

  • Follow up with new inquiries and convert prospective patients into booked appointments.
  • Proactively reconnect with inactive patients, lost leads, and previous inquiries to generate new sales opportunities.
  • Conduct outbound calls and consistent follow-ups to encourage appointment bookings and treatment purchases.
  • Explain available treatments and packages using approved information and sales guidelines.
  • Confidently ask for the sale and help close treatment or package purchases.
  • Send secure payment links, monitor payment status, and follow up on outstanding deposits or purchases.
  • Maintain a warm, persuasive, and professional approach throughout the sales process.
  • Track lead conversions, appointment bookings, and sales performance against agreed goals.

2. Phone Coverage & Patient Communication (Top Priority)

  • Answer incoming and overflow calls using RingCentral.
  • Respond to patient inquiries promptly and professionally.
  • Provide accurate general information about services, appointments, and next steps.
  • Build rapport with prospective and existing patients through friendly, confident communication.
  • Direct clinical or other specialized inquiries to the appropriate staff members.
  • Document important call details and ensure timely follow-ups.

3. CRM Management & Administrative Support (Top Priority)

  • Maintain accurate patient and lead information in Aesthetic Record CRM.
  • Update lead statuses, document calls, and track follow-up activities.
  • Schedule appointments and maintain an organized practice calendar.
  • Monitor appointment readiness and coordinate necessary follow-ups.
  • Organize sales pipelines and identify leads requiring additional outreach.
  • Provide general administrative and back-office support as needed.

Sales & Lead Management

You'll work with an established database of prospective and existing patients, including:

  • Approximately 5–10 new leads per day, depending on marketing activity.
  • An existing database of approximately 1,000 contacts for follow-up and reactivation.
  • Leads generated through marketing campaigns, social media, email, and other practice channels.

You will not be responsible for sourcing or purchasing lead lists. The client provides leads through Aesthetic Record.

Outbound outreach and lead reactivation will be especially important during the initial part-time arrangement. Lead volumes may increase as marketing campaigns expand, and prompt responses to new leads will be a key priority.

Tools & Platforms

  • Aesthetic Record CRM: Lead management, patient records, appointment scheduling, and follow-up tracking. Training will be provided.
  • RingCentral: Incoming and outgoing calls, patient communication, and sales outreach.

What Success Looks Like

  • Consistently converting qualified inquiries into booked appointments.
  • Proactively reactivating inactive leads and generating treatment sales.
  • Following through on sales opportunities, payment links, and outstanding deposits.
  • Maintaining professional, welcoming communication with every patient.
  • Keeping CRM records, lead statuses, and follow-up activities accurate and updated.
  • Meeting agreed appointment conversion and sales performance goals.
  • Managing responsibilities independently and adapting to the practice's evolving needs.

Requirements

Required Skills & Experience

  • Proven sales experience with demonstrated closing ability.
  • Hands-on experience with appointment setting, lead follow-up, and sales conversion.
  • Experience conducting outbound calls, proactive outreach, and cold calling.
  • Ability to reactivate inactive leads and confidently pursue sales opportunities.
  • Excellent verbal and written English communication skills.
  • Strong phone etiquette with a friendly, warm, persuasive, and professional approach.
  • Confidence explaining products or services, overcoming objections, and asking for the sale.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail when maintaining CRM records and tracking follow-ups.
  • Ability to manage multiple leads, prioritize opportunities, and work toward performance targets.
  • Willingness to learn the client's treatments, packages, sales scripts, and established processes.
  • Familiarity with customer confidentiality and willingness to follow HIPAA requirements.
  • Proactive, persistent, self-motivated, reliable, and comfortable working independently.
  • Willingness to transition from part-time to full-time as business needs grow.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous experience in medical spas, aesthetics, healthcare sales, or a related industry.
  • Familiarity with Aesthetic Record CRM or similar medical spa/aesthetics platforms.
  • Experience selling treatments, service packages, memberships, or other high-value offerings.
  • Experience managing large lead databases and reactivation campaigns.
  • Experience handling patient inquiries, appointment scheduling, and front-desk support.
  • Spanish-English bilingual proficiency is highly preferred but not required.

Candidates with strong sales closing experience from other industries are encouraged to apply. Proven sales ability and excellent English communication are more important than industry-specific experience or bilingual proficiency.

Ideal Candidate Profile

We're looking for someone who is:

  • A Confident Sales Closer: Comfortable asking for the sale, overcoming objections, and turning inquiries into paying customers.
  • Persistent & Results-Driven: Motivated to follow up consistently and convert inactive leads into new opportunities.
  • Warm & Personable: Creates a welcoming experience while building trust and rapport with prospective patients.
  • Proactive & Independent: Takes ownership of the sales pipeline and identifies opportunities without constant supervision.
  • Highly Organized: Maintains accurate CRM records, schedules, and follow-up activities.
  • Adaptable & Coachable: Learns new systems and services quickly and applies feedback effectively.
  • Reliable & Accountable: Consistently follows through on commitments and works toward agreed performance goals.

Basic Requirements

  • Must be proficient in speaking and writing clear, professional English.
  • Must have relevant sales experience, including appointment setting and closing.
  • Must be comfortable handling inbound and outbound calls.
  • Must be available Monday–Friday, 10:00 AM–2:00 PM Pacific Time.
  • Must be open to potentially increasing working hours to full-time.
  • Must be able to submit an NBI Clearance and/or Local Police Clearance before onboarding (mandatory).
  • Must be available for video meetings with camera on when required.

Technical Requirements

  • Computer: Reliable laptop or desktop computer.
  • Internet: Stable high-speed internet connection (minimum 25 Mbps).
  • Audio: Noise-canceling headset.
  • Video: Working webcam for virtual meetings.
  • Workspace: Quiet and professional work environment.

Benefits

  • Dedicated HR & Contractor Support Team: Access to world-class support for questions, guidance, contract matters, and client communication.
  • Premium VPN Access (Optional): A secure VPN license can be provided upon request to enhance privacy and security for client-related tasks.
  • HIPAA & Cybersecurity Training + Certification (Provided): Access to our internal HIPAA compliance training, cybersecurity modules, and certification to help you confidently handle PHI for U.S. healthcare clients.
  • Top 1% VA Performance Training: Access to our proprietary training on communication, client management, productivity systems, and best practices to help you become a top-performing VA and increase long-term client retention.
  • Client-Approved U.S. Holidays: Contractors may take U.S. holidays off according to the client’s needs and schedule.
  • Client-Approved Paid or Unpaid Time Off: Time off may be granted by your client. Paid time off is optional and only if offered by the client.
  • Access to Tools & Resources: Templates, workflow guides, productivity tools, and client-specific SOP support to help you perform at your best.
  • Optional Performance-Based Incentives: Some clients may offer bonuses, incentives, or increased hours based on your performance.

These are optional resources and client-approved allowances available to you as an independent contractor. Any resources, training, or allowances listed are optional contractor perks and not employee benefits.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Full Stack
jobs.excerpt: Lyric is the trusted leader in healthcare decision intelligence.
jobs.description:
Lyric is the trusted leader in healthcare decision intelligence. Built on more than 35 years of proven results, Lyric combines responsible AI with clinical, payment, regulatory, and policy expertise to deliver transparent, auditable insights in milliseconds across real-time claims workflows. Lyric augments human decision-making so health plans can make faster, more accurate payments while maintaining full control. Today, Lyric supports 200 million lives, with nine of the top 10 U.S. health plans relying on its platform to reduce waste, improve efficiency, and support accurate payments.

Applicants must already be legally authorized to work in the U.S. Visa sponsorship/sponsorship assumption and other immigration support are not available for this position.

We’re a company at the intersection of FinTech and Healthcare, committed to simplifying healthcare payment integrity and creating value for health insurers, healthcare providers, and consumers. We’re not a startup, but we move like one when it matters. Right now, we’re in the middle of a serious modernization of our payment integrity platform: replacing legacy .NET, rebuilding the experience layer around modern web frameworks, fixing data bottlenecks, and getting the product ready to scale.

We’re hiring a Full Stack Engineer whose center of gravity is the front end. You’ll spend most of your time designing and building the web experiences our customers actually live in – modular Angular applications, micro-frontend architecture, design systems, accessibility, performance, and the kind of interaction quality that makes a complex product feel simple. You’ll also reach into the backend with confidence: shaping the .NET APIs your UI depends on, tuning the queries that feed your screens, and making sure the seams between client and server are clean. You’ll work closely with product, UX, and DevOps to ship customer-delighting features at scale.

Here’s what makes this role different: you’re not just a frontend engineer who “also knows AI.” We want someone who has already figured out that tools like Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex aren’t toys – they’re force multipliers. You’ll use AI agents every day to tear through component refactors, framework upgrades, test coverage, and the backend work that comes with full-stack ownership. But you also know when the AI is wrong, when to step in, and how to keep quality high. Think of it as having a junior engineer with infinite energy and zero judgment – your job is to supply the judgment.

ESSENTIAL JOB RESPONSIBILITIES & KEY PERFORMANCE OUTCOMES

Lead the front-end modernization of the product

This is the bulk of what you’ll do. You’ll:

  • Design and build React applications that are modular, testable, and accessible by default – with a real point of view on component architecture, state management, routing, and shared libraries.

  • Own the experience layer end to end: design system contributions, responsive layouts, accessibility (WCAG), client-side performance, error and loading states, and the small details that separate a workflow people tolerate from one they trust.

  • Partner with UX on flows that hold up under real customer workloads – dense tables, long-running operations, complex permissioning – not just happy-path mockups.

What success looks like:

  • Customers notice the difference. Workflows feel faster, clearer, and more reliable, and the screens that used to generate support tickets stop generating them.

  • The front-end codebase becomes something the team is proud of: consistent patterns, real test coverage, stable build and release tooling, and a design system that other engineers actually reach for instead of reinventing.

Deliver full-stack features against a real .NET + PostgreSQL stack

Your features don’t stop at the API boundary. You’ll:

  • Shape and extend the .NET APIs your front end consumes – RESTful, versioned, and built for correctness and maintainability, not just “it works.”

  • Make pragmatic backend changes: adding endpoints, refactoring service boundaries, tightening contracts, and replacing legacy .NET code where it’s blocking the experience you’re trying to ship.

  • Get your hands into SQL when the UI demands it – query performance, indexing, transactional correctness – and contribute to data pipelines (Kafka, event-driven flows) when the work calls for it.

What success looks like:

  • You ship features end to end without needing a backend engineer to hand-hold each one. Critical paths land in modern code, sprint over sprint.

  • APIs that back your UIs get faster and more reliable. Database hot spots stop waking people up at night.

Ship modernization work at a pace that surprises people

This is your superpower. You’ll:

  • Use AI agents (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex) to power through component migrations, framework upgrades, API extraction, test scaffolding, and documentation – while catching hallucinations and preventing regressions before they hit a PR.

  • Build reusable playbooks the team can actually follow: prompt templates, repo-level agent instructions, migration checklists, review heuristics, and clear “definition of done” standards for AI-assisted changes – on both the front-end and backend sides of the codebase.

What success looks like:

  • You measurably move the needle – more modules migrated per sprint, faster PR turnarounds – without a spike in production bugs.

  • The team gets better because of you: PRs are clearer, test coverage grows, documentation stays current, and the same mistakes stop repeating.

Own it like it’s yours – especially because this is healthcare

You’ll:

  • Build with security and privacy as defaults, not afterthoughts – both on the client (safe data handling, careful state, sensible telemetry) and on the server (least privilege, auditability). This is healthcare. Getting it wrong isn’t an option.

  • Put real quality guardrails in place: component and integration tests, end-to-end coverage on the flows that matter, CI that blocks bad changes, structured logging, and front-end observability that tells you what users actually experience before they tell you.

  • Review code thoughtfully, have honest architectural conversations, and raise the bar without being a jerk about it.

What success looks like:

  • Fewer severity-1 incidents. When something does go wrong, root cause takes minutes, not hours.

  • Automated test coverage grows meaningfully on modernized code – across the UI, the API layer, and the integration seam between them. The team stops relying on “just test it manually.”

Work with real humans to ship things that matter

You’ll:

  • Partner with analysts, stakeholders, designers, and other engineers to turn business problems into working software – not just technically correct software, but software that actually solves the problem.

  • Help build delivery plans that are honest about trade-offs. “Right” vs. “right now” is a real tension – you’ll help the team navigate it with pragmatic milestones.

What success looks like:

  • Delivery is predictable. Customer onboarding milestones are met. Features ship with confidence, not crossed fingers.

REQUIRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

  • 5+ years building and shipping production systems. Not side projects – real software with real users. You’re able to work independently and collaboratively in fast-moving teams.

  • Deep front-end experience with React/Next.js (or comparable depth in Angular with a willingness to lead in React). You’ve built and maintained non-trivial applications: component architecture, state management, routing, forms, accessibility, and performance. You’ve worked at the scale where shared libraries and design systems become real problems – not slides.

  • Strong fundamentals across the modern web platform: TypeScript, HTML, CSS, browser performance, accessibility, testing (unit, component, end-to-end), and the build/release tooling that goes with it.

  • Solid working experience with C# and modern .NET (Core and beyond). You don’t need to be the deepest backend engineer in the room, but you can confidently read, extend, and refactor service code – and you’ve done meaningful work in real codebases, not just greenfield.

  • Comfortable with SQL – enough to design reasonable schemas, write and tune the queries your UI depends on, and recognize when a performance problem belongs at the database, not the client.

  • API design experience – you’ve built and consumed service-oriented APIs with real versioning, auth, reliability, and testing practices, and you have opinions about what makes a backend pleasant (or painful) to integrate with from a front end.

  • Cloud experience with AWS and/or Azure. AWS is particularly relevant here.

  • You actually use AI coding tools as a daily driver. Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or similar – and not just for autocomplete. You’ve used agents for multi-file refactors, migrations, test generation, and review workflows. You have opinions about what works and what doesn’t.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • You’ve led or played a significant role in a real front-end modernization – AngularJS to React, jQuery to a modern framework, a monolithic UI to micro-frontends, or similar. You know where the bodies are buried and you have the scars to prove it.

  • Deep design system or component library experience – you’ve built one, contributed substantially to one, or hauled a team off a tangle of one-off components onto something coherent.

  • You’ve done a legacy ASP.NET / .NET Framework modernization on the backend side.

  • Experience with distributed systems tooling – Kafka, event-driven architectures, or working with Postgres alongside SQL Server.

  • You’ve helped establish agent-friendly engineering practices: writing repo instructions that AI tools can follow, breaking work into agent-sized tasks, setting up CI guardrails for AI-generated code, feature flags, canary deployments – any part of the progressive delivery toolkit.

  • You communicate clearly. Good PR descriptions, straightforward design docs, pragmatic collaboration, low ego. We don’t need a rockstar – we need someone the team trusts.

  • Background in regulated domains (healthcare, fintech, payments) where “move fast and break things” will get you fired.

You'll use AI agents every day to tear through migrations, refactors, and test coverage that would take a traditional team weeks. But you also know when the AI is wrong, when to step in, and how to keep quality high. Think of it as having a junior engineer with infinite energy and zero judgment - your job is to supply the judgment.

ESSENTIAL JOB RESPONSIBILITIES & KEY PERFORMANCE OUTCOMES

Ship modernization work at a pace that surprises people

This is your superpower. You'll:

  • Use AI agents (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex) to blow through framework upgrades, refactors, API extraction, test scaffolding, and documentation - while catching hallucinations and preventing regressions before they hit a PR.

  • Build reusable playbooks the team can actually follow: prompt templates, repo-level agent instructions, migration checklists, review heuristics, and clear "definition of done" standards for AI-assisted changes.

What success looks like:

  • You measurably move the needle - more modules migrated per sprint, faster PR turnarounds - without a spike in production bugs.

  • The team gets better because of you: PRs are clearer, test coverage grows, documentation stays current, and the same mistakes stop repeating.

Modernize a real .NET + SQL Server stack into something you'd be proud of

You'll:

  • Upgrade legacy services to current .NET (LTS where it makes sense), untangling architecture boundaries and fixing the performance issues that have been "known" for years.

  • Push toward a proper API-layer architecture - RESTful, versioned - built for correctness and maintainability, not just "it works."

  • Get your hands dirty with SQL Server: query performance, indexing, transactional correctness. If there are data pipeline needs (Kafka, etc.), you'll help build those too.

What success looks like:

  • Legacy surface area shrinks sprint over sprint. Critical paths live in modern code. Fewer "oh, that's still in the old system" conversations.

  • APIs get faster and more reliable. Database hot spots stop waking people up at night.

Own it like it's yours - especially because this is healthcare

You'll:

  • Build with security and privacy as defaults, not afterthoughts. Least privilege, safe data handling, the works. This is healthcare - getting it wrong isn't an option.

  • Put real quality guardrails in place: automated tests that actually catch things, CI that blocks bad changes, structured logging, observability that tells you what's happening before users do.

  • Review code thoughtfully, have honest architectural conversations, and raise the bar without being a jerk about it.

What success looks like:

  • Fewer severity-1 incidents. When something does go wrong, root cause takes hours, not days.

  • Automated test coverage grows meaningfully on modernized code. The team stops relying on "just test it manually."

Work with real humans to ship things that matter

You'll:

  • Partner with analysts, stakeholders, and other engineers to turn business problems into working software - not just technically correct software, but software that actually solves the problem.

  • Help build delivery plans that are honest about trade-offs. "Right" vs. "right now" is a real tension - you'll help the team navigate it with pragmatic milestones.

What success looks like:

  • Delivery is predictable. Customer onboarding milestones are met. Features ship with confidence, not crossed fingers.

REQUIRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

  • 5+ years building and shipping production systems. Not side projects - real software with real users.solving skills; able to work independently and collaboratively in fastmoving teams

  • Some C# and modern .NET experience (Core and beyond). Especially in large codebases and you've done meaningful refactoring and migration work, not just greenfield.

  • Strong SQL Server chops - schema design, query tuning, performance troubleshooting. You've worked on data-heavy applications where the database wasn't an afterthought.

  • Cloud experience with Azure and/or AWS. Azure is particularly relevant here.

  • API design experience - you've built and maintained service-oriented architectures with real versioning, auth, reliability, and testing practices.

  • You actually use AI coding tools as a daily driver. Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or similar - and not just for autocomplete. You've used agents for multi-file refactors, migrations, test generation, and review workflows. You have opinions about what works and what doesn't.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • You've actually done a legacy ASP.NET / .NET Framework modernization before. You know where the bodies are buried and you have the scars to prove it. Bonus points for Azure modernization patterns.

  • You communicate clearly. Good PR descriptions, straightforward design docs, pragmatic collaboration, low ego. We don't need a rockstar - we need someone the team trusts.

  • Experience with distributed systems tooling - Kafka, event-driven architectures, or working with Postgres alongside SQL Server.

  • Front-end experience with Angular and/or React/Next.js.

  • You've helped establish agent-friendly engineering practices: writing repo instructions that AI tools can follow, breaking work into agent-sized tasks, setting up CI guardrails for AI-generated code, feature flags, canary deployments - any part of the progressive delivery toolkit.

  • Background in regulated domains (healthcare, fintech, payments) where "move fast and break things" will get you fired.

The selected candidate will design, develop, and maintain Power BI dashboards, reports, data models, and performance scorecards that provide accurate visibility of IT assets, configuration items, infrastructure health, lifecycle status, service delivery, and contract key performance indicators (KPIs). jobs.description:
We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production. That means orchestrating multi-step workflows with retries, skips, and parallel execution; keeping long-running work persistent and observable; and serving per-tenant retrieval at scale. This isn't about wrapping an LLM in an API call, it's the hard backend engineering that makes agents dependable.

Our stack is Python (FastAPI) on AWS, with Terraform. We hire on engineering depth and judgment, not on a keyword count, and we work in whichever language you're strongest in during the interview (more below). As a Senior Engineer, you will own backend services and the orchestration layer on top of them, from design through deployment, operation, and the on-call that follows.

Our team is based in Tehran and pays salaries monthly in USD.

What You Will Do:

  • Design, build, and own backend services and the agent-orchestration layer end to end.

  • Build resilient systems that stay correct under load and degrade gracefully when a model, tool, or dependency fails.

  • Ensure operational excellence by making long-running, multi-step work observable and debuggable in production.

  • Shape technical direction through rigorous code reviews, mentorship, and pushing back on specifications when they misalign with engineering reality.

  • Drive the full software development lifecycle, translating ambiguous requirements into durable architectures and actionable technical plans.

What We Are Looking For:

  • 5+ years building and operating production backend systems, with deep ownership of at least one non-trivial service you can talk through end to end.

  • Deep fluency in your primary backend language, and the ability to pick up a new one fast. We work in Python; if it is not your daily language today, we expect you to ramp quickly.

  • Strong systems fundamentals — concurrency, data modeling, and failure modes — and the judgment to choose the right abstraction rather than the cleverest one.

  • Sound reasoning under ambiguity: you ask the clarifying question first, make the trade-offs explicit, and adapt when the constraints change.

  • Solid grasp of infrastructure and operations, including message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ), SQL and NoSQL stores, and running services in containers with an orchestrator (Kubernetes, ECS, Nomad, or similar).

  • Professional written English, enabling you to write crisp design documents and align stakeholders on complex technical trade-offs.

Even Better:

  • AWS (especially ECS) and Terraform, or comparable cloud and Infrastructure-as-Code experience.

  • Hands-on work with LLM, agentic, or RAG systems (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs, Hugging Face) and a real grasp of how non-deterministic agent steps differ from ordinary functions.

  • A recognized-bar engineering background, owned open-source work, or another verifiable standout signal.

How We Hire:

We use a deliberate, transparent two-stage process designed to see how you think and build:

About BookNook:

BookNook is a research-driven high-impact tutoring solution that supports K–8 students in reading and math through live, synchronous tutoring sessions. Partnering with school districts and nonprofit organizations nationwide, BookNook delivers standards-aligned 1:1 or small-group instruction and structured tutoring models designed to strengthen foundational skills and accelerate student learning.

Since 2016, BookNook has supported more than 2.7K schools and partners across 40 states. Independent research demonstrates a clear link between high-impact tutoring and improved student outcomes. BookNook is committed to expanding access to strong academic support by connecting schools with skilled, supported tutors and scalable delivery models. Learn more at

Employment Type: Full-Time, W-2 permanent position

Data at BookNook:

Data at BookNook powers how we measure and communicate the impact of tutoring, and how districts, states, and research partners come to understand it. From state reporting feeds to the outcomes districts share with their school boards, we turn session and assessment data into insights for our customers, partners, and teams. We favor simple solutions to complex problems, build for scale over one-off answers, and treat student data with the care and responsibility it deserves.

This role will own that work end to end, evolving our data platform and driving data-informed decisions across BookNook to keep us at the forefront of high-impact tutoring.

The Role:

As BookNook’s Senior Analytics Engineer, you’ll own our data platform and the reporting built on it, delivering the state, district, and partner reporting our customers depend on. This is a hands-on technical role. You’ll administer our Snowflake environment, write and maintain the Python automations that power our reporting, and decide how our data is structured and managed. Your first year centers on the platform, state data feeds, and recurring client reporting. From there, you’ll lay the groundwork for longitudinal, year-over-year research on student outcomes and scalable operational reporting for executive leadership. You’ll be accountable not just for building our reporting, but for making sure people across BookNook actually use it and that it keeps getting better.

This is a senior Individual Contributor (IC) role, and you’ll be the dedicated owner of BookNook’s data function. You’ll report to the VP of Product Strategy and partner closely with engineering, security and IT, implementations, tutor operations, and executive leadership. As our data needs grow, you’ll help shape what the data function becomes.

About You:

You’re an experienced analytics or data engineer who is comfortable being the person who owns the data. You’re comfortable making decisions about how data is modeled, stored, and moved, pushing back thoughtfully on requests that won’t scale, and setting your own priorities. When someone asks for a number, you want to know what they’re trying to learn or decide, and you dig into what we actually have to find the closest honest answer, even when it isn’t the exact thing they asked for.

You can explain what the data shows, and what it doesn’t, to people who aren’t technical. You’re just as comfortable walking a district data team through a report as you are writing a pipeline, and you’d rather automate a process once than run it by hand every week. You build repeatable patterns rather than one-off analyses, so the answer to a question gets easier the second time someone asks it. You understand student data privacy standards, and you hold yourself to a standard that goes beyond what the law requires. You care about impact on the business and on the students and educators who rely on BookNook every day.

What you will be doing:

  • Data Platform Ownership: Own BookNook’s Snowflake environment and account, including cost and capacity management, data modeling, and the pipelines that turn raw data into reporting. Our SRE manages the pipeline from our production database into Snowflake, and you’ll partner closely with them as we move toward more real-time reporting.
  • End-to-End Project Ownership: Own data projects from the first question through delivery and upkeep, whether that’s a new state data feed, an automation, or a research dataset. Lead scoping conversations with stakeholders and present results internally as BookNook’s subject-matter expert on our data.
  • Data Privacy and Security: Make sure our company data privacy and PII policies are applied correctly across Snowflake and our other reporting tools and processes, and help enforce them. Partner closely with our IT and security team and our SRE to shape those policies at a company level, not just how they apply to our data stack.
  • Internal Data Partnership: Be the bridge between what people across BookNook ask for and what our data can actually answer. Understand the question behind each request, and help people move past data points that won’t support what they’re trying to show. Explain your findings clearly, including their limits, to non-technical audiences. Help teams across BookNook use our reports and tools on their own, so fewer requests need you.
  • Pipelines and Automation: Maintain and extend the automation engines, scheduled tasks, and one-click exports that support our customer-facing teams, including the tools that deliver data to states and partners, like SFTP and Airbyte. Continually find new places to remove manual data work from people’s plates, using scripts to bridge the gap where full automation isn’t in place yet.
  • Technical Partnerships and Reporting: Build strong working relationships with district admin and IT teams and with state data teams, staying current on state guidance and the data sharing requirements our partners need to meet to receive funding. Own state data feeds and district and partner reporting from start to finish, including custom data pulls, saved views, BI report builds, and the documentation that goes with them.
  • Onboarding and Process Improvement: Partner with engineering and implementations to design and refine processes for customer onboarding and ongoing reporting, especially for large customers, including reporting that helps validate setup and data quality.
  • Research and Partnerships Data: Build and maintain the foundations for outcomes research, including our assessment results data and tutor efficacy reporting. Lead the work to support longitudinal, year-over-year studies with research partners.
  • Operational Analytics: Provide executive leadership with the operational data they need and help scale dashboarding across the business. Use what you learn to propose improvements to the BookNook platform and services.

What we are looking for:

  • Experience: 5+ years in analytics engineering, data engineering, or a similar role, including time as the primary owner of a data platform, ideally at a small or growing company.
  • Snowflake Proficiency: Strong SQL skills and hands-on experience administering and building in Snowflake, including access control, cost management, and performance.
  • Python and Automation: Experience writing and maintaining Python scripts that run on a schedule to pull, transform, and deliver data, like automated reports, exports, and data feeds to partners.
  • BI and Reporting: Advanced experience building reports and dashboards in a BI tool such as Tableau, Power BI, Astrato, or similar.
  • Business and Data Judgment: The curiosity to learn our business model, our market, and how we work with districts, states, and partners well enough to know what our data can and can’t tell us, and to find a defensible answer when the exact one doesn’t exist.
  • Data Privacy: A working understanding of FERPA and related student privacy obligations, and a clear point of view on protecting data about minors.
  • Ownership and Prioritization: Comfort making decisions about how our data is modeled, stored, secured, and moved, prioritizing your own work, and saying no when a request doesn’t fit.
  • Communication and Relationships: Ability to explain technical concepts, findings, and tradeoffs to non-technical audiences, and to build strong relationships with internal teams and external partners, including district IT staff and state data teams.

Nice to have:

  • Experience in educational technology, specifically in K-12 environments.
  • Familiarity with educational assessments (such as i-Ready, DIBELS, or STAR) and the messiness of district-provided data.
  • Experience with data sharing and integration tools, such as SFTP and connectors like Airbyte.
  • Experience with real-time or streaming data pipelines.
  • Experience supporting research studies or longitudinal analysis.

We know imposter syndrome can sometimes discourage candidates from applying for jobs. If this role would make you excited to come to work every day, we encourage you to apply even if you don't meet all the requirements.

Perks and Benefits

  • Competitive salary: For this role, the salary range is $130K to $160K. Exact compensation may vary based on skills and experience.
  • Work remotely: Live and work wherever you like in the continental US.
  • Health insurance: We offer medical, dental, and vision insurance for all our team members.
  • Time to recharge: We offer flexible PTO, 11 paid holidays, and one company-wide week off.
  • 401(k): With 3% company match.
  • Home office setup: Get a laptop + $130 monthly stipend for home expenses.
  • Employee Recognition: We have built a culture based upon recognizing our coworkers’ value based achievements.

jobs.excerpt: About Positron AI Positron AI is building next-generation AI inference accelerators designed from the ground up for low-latency, high-throughput large language model inference.
jobs.description:
About Positron AI

Positron AI is building next-generation AI inference accelerators designed from the ground up for low-latency, high-throughput large language model inference. Chips built for the training era keep running into two walls at inference time: memory bandwidth and chip-to-chip networking. We designed our architecture to break through both. Our first-generation Atlas systems are already in production on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Asimov, our first custom ASIC, takes that architecture to silicon. In simulations, Asimov delivers several times more tokens per dollar and tokens per watt than leading GPUs, at a fraction of the power. Paired in our Titan system, Asimov is built to serve models beyond 16 trillion parameters. In September 2026, we raised $875 million at a $5 billion valuation. NEA led the round, joined by Atreides Management, Valor Equity Partners, and others, to bring Asimov and Titan to market. Our team includes engineers from Groq, Lambda, NVIDIA, Meta, F5, and many other industry leaders.

Role Overview

As a Developer Platform Engineer, you will build the layer that lets AI coding agents do real work on our simulators. We have a full simulation ecosystem built on one shared hardware model, and demand on it is growing in every direction at once: more chip programs, new model architectures, larger deployment topologies, and customers who want modeling tooling. We cannot scale by adding people alone. You will work with every engineer on the team to make routine simulator work, such as adding commands, running experiments, and bringing up new models, something an agent can do end to end, with evidence.

The work is platform engineering with a verification mindset: the interfaces agents call, the workflows they follow, and the guardrails that keep agent-written changes trustworthy. Our test lead continues to own testing practice; you will build the agent layer on top of it.

Key Responsibilities

Agent Interfaces

  • Design and build the MCP servers and APIs that let AI coding agents drive our simulators end to end, so that running a simulation, reading a trace, and comparing against a reference all happen from one call.
  • Make the simulators legible to agents and people alike through clear CLI and API design, structured outputs, reproducible runs, and useful error messages.

Agent Workflows

  • Build agent workflows for simulator development in which an agent implements or extends a hardware command's functional, dependency, cost, and cycle models and lands it with test evidence.
  • Partner with the model architecture engineer to automate new-model bring-up from model specification to simulator coverage.

Guardrails and Measurement

  • Build CI guardrails for agent-produced changes, including golden-reference generation, static analysis, known-good comparisons, and provenance on every result.
  • Measure what agents get right and wrong, and feed those findings back into the tooling.

Required Qualifications

  • 4+ years of experience in developer tooling, developer platforms, or infrastructure engineering.
  • Demonstrated experience building tooling that LLM coding agents use in production, such as MCP servers or tool APIs, agent workflows in CI, evaluation harnesses, or agent-driven code generation with verification.
  • A strong understanding of CI/CD and test infrastructure, including flaky-test detection, golden-reference testing, and static analysis in CI.
  • Hands-on experience designing CLIs and APIs that are easy to use correctly and hard to use wrongly, with structured logging and reproducible builds.
  • Ability to design systems in which agent-produced changes carry evidence and cannot land unverified.
  • Strong Rust skills, or expert-level C/C++ skills and a willingness to work in Rust day to day, along with proficiency in Python for tooling.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain to engineers what the agent layer can and cannot be trusted with, and why.

Preferred Qualifications

  • A background in simulation, compilers, or hardware.
  • Experience running evaluations of agent or model performance on engineering tasks.

Leveling & Scope

While this role is currently posted at a specific level, we are a growth-oriented organization and are open to hiring at a more senior level for the right candidate. Please note that this job description serves as a focused but generalized overview of the role; specific responsibilities and impact expectations will be tailored to the experience and seniority of the final hire.

Why Join Us?

  • You will define how AI coding agents do trustworthy engineering work on a real chip simulation stack, a problem few teams anywhere are tackling in production.
  • Your tooling will multiply the output of every engineer on the team as we scale across chip programs, model architectures, and customers.

Compensation & Benefits

The base salary range for this role is Mid: $160,000-$220,000, Senior: $220,000–$270,000, Principal: $270,000-$350,000.

Please note that the figures provided represent the base salary range only and do not include other elements of our total compensation package, equity, or comprehensive benefits.

At Positron AI, we value the unique expertise each candidate brings. While the range above reflects our typical expectation for the position, we reserve the flexibility to exceed this range for candidates whose specialized skills, significant experience, or unique qualifications fall outside the standard scope of the role. Final offers are determined based on a variety of factors, including internal equity, and individual impact.

Benefits & Perks

We want you to do your best work and feel confident that you and your family are taken care of. That means comprehensive coverage, real time to rest, and support for your future.

Health and wellness

  • Fully company-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance for you and your dependents
  • Company-paid life and disability coverage, with voluntary options to add more
  • Supplemental hospital, critical illness, and accident coverage available

Time off and flexibility

  • Unlimited paid time off; we encourage everyone to truly unplug and recharge
  • 13 paid company holidays
  • Remote-first culture with a company-provided computer and home office setup

Compensation and future

  • Competitive salary and equity
  • 401(k) with company matching, eligible from day one

Visa Support

This position is open to candidates currently authorized to work in the U.S. We cannot provide new visa sponsorship for this role but are open to facilitating H-1B visa transfers for eligible candidates.

Equal Opportunity Employer. If you're excited about the role but don't meet every bullet, we'd still love to hear from you.

jobs.description:
About the Company:

The mining industry has steadily become worse at finding new ore deposits, requiring >10X more capital to make discoveries compared to 30 years ago. The easy-to-find, near-surface deposits have largely been found, and the industry has chronically under-invested in new exploration technology, relying on the manual techniques of yesteryear – even as demand accelerates for copper, lithium, and other metals to build electric vehicles, renewable energy, and data centers.

KoBold builds AI models for mineral exploration and deploys those models—alongside our novel sensors—to guide decisions on KoBold-owned-and-operated exploration programs. Since our founding in 2018, KoBold has become by far both the largest independent mineral exploration company and the largest exploration technology developer. Our data scientists and software engineers, who come from leading technology companies, jointly lead exploration programs with our renowned exploration geologists.

KoBold has proven its first discovery with materially less capital than the industry average and found one of the best copper deposits ever discovered: the copper is far more concentrated than the global average of copper mines, and this asset alone is expected to generate meaningful revenue for decades. KoBold has a portfolio of more than 80 other projects, each of which has the potential for another high-quality discovery.

KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.

About the position

In this role, you will lead evaluations of potential properties for acquisition, generate targets, and design and oversee field programs from target definition through to resource expansion. You will be part of a multidisciplinary team and will work closely with data scientists, using KoBold’s technology to help guide our field programs and decision-making. You will also work directly with our senior technical advisors and with the executive team on making the investment case for acquisitions and field programs.

Ultimately, your role is to help KoBold make valuable discoveries by identifying opportunities with rigorous evaluation and by ensuring that we safely and effectively conduct our field programs.

Responsibilities
  • Demonstrate in all activities a commitment to the highest standards in health and safety, environment, and community relations
  • Rigorously analyze geoscientific datasets across a range of scales from provinces to prospects to determine exploration potential and to identify, rank, and prioritize exploration targets
  • Design, budget, permit, and execute field programs ranging from geological mapping and sampling of grass roots prospects through to large drilling programs on advanced projects, with leading industry practice in data acquisition and validation
  • Provide technical guidance and support to local in-country project teams during the design and execution of exploration programs, including site visits and engagement with other project stakeholders (e.g., community representatives, regulatory authorities, and joint venture partners)
  • Work collaboratively with data scientist colleagues to conceive and implement insightful analytical methods
Qualifications

A great Exploration Geologist candidate will have:

  • Strong technical knowledge of one or more ore deposit types. Experience working on sediment-hosted stratiform copper or magmatic sulfide deposits will be considered an advantage
  • Excellence in generative analysis ranging from new concepts to integration, interpretation, and modeling of large datasets
  • Good field skills and experience conducting field programs across a range of project stages from grassroots prospects through to advanced projects with significant drilling campaigns
  • Baseline level of proficiency in standard desktop software packages (e.g., ArcGIS or QGIS)
  • Strong leadership skills including the ability to motivate and inspire others, to share ownership and responsibility for project outcomes, and to work effectively in collaborative, interdisciplinary teams
  • Previous experience in coaching and training geoscientists of varying experience, educational backgrounds and cultures in leading-practice mineral exploration
  • Demonstrated commitment to high standards of health and safety in the workplace
  • A minimum of 3-7 years experience in the mineral exploration industry
  • A valid passport (or the ability to obtain one) and willingness to travel to Mingomba or other exploration sites worldwide.

It is helpful but not required to have:

  • Working knowledge of one programming or scripting language (e.g., Python, R, C/C++)
  • Knowledge of geostatistics and/or other statistical methods relevant for analysis of geoscientific data
  • International experience, particularly in the Central African Copperbelt

Note: Candidates who are specialists in geochemistry or geophysics but open to doing significant project work are encouraged to apply.

What to Expect

Joining KoBold means getting the opportunity for hands-on exposure to our exploration projects around the world. All employees are expected to travel to project sites, with a minimum of one week per year. Field-facing and technical roles spend significantly more time in the field.

KoBold Metals is an equal opportunity workplace and an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity for people of any race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, age, citizenship, disability, or veteran status.

The US base salary range for this full-time exempt position is $70,000-$110,000.

Location: KoBold is a remote-first workplace. All candidates must be legally authorized to work in one of the following countries: United States, Canada, Australia, South Africa, United Kingdom, Zambia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Namibia, Finland, Sweden, or Botswana.

Title: Senior DatabaseEngineer — Oracle & Distributed Data Systems (Cleared)

The environment: Amission-critical, geographically distributed system serving the IntelligenceCommunity — one where interface, performance, and security tolerances are tightand non-negotiable. You'll be a database engineering voice on a complexprogram, not a ticket-taker.
What you'll own:
  • Relational and non-relational data architecture — design, build, and document
  • Data movement at scale: replication across distributed nodes, concurrent access, failover and high-availability engineering
  • Performance work: tuning, capacity and performance planning, issue investigation through resolution
  • Backup, recovery, and user administration
  • Schema translation — turning requirements and raw data into usable structures via ad hoc queries, scripts, and macros
  • Requirements analysis, risk assessment, and alternatives analysis for system-level problems
  • Long- and short-term database requirements for admin and design

Requirements

How you'll work: Embeddedin an Agile team, interfacing with systems, software, test, and informationassurance engineers. You'll contribute to Program Increment Planning andcollaborate daily with technical peers and customer POCs.

Clearance (hard gate): ActiveTS/SCI with Full Scope Polygraph through the MD customer. Last poly within 6years. No CCAs.
Experience bar:
  • 10+ years as a DBA on similar-scope programs
  • Oracle SQL/PLSQL plus general SQL — strong
  • Exposure to relational and NoSQL engines (PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Cassandra)
  • Scripting: Python, Perl, Bash/Linux shell, and/or JavaScript
  • Java as a language baseline
  • Technical bachelor's, or 4 years additional DBA experience in lieu

Nice to have: SAFemethodology or Agile team experience; Cassandra; MongoDB.

Sometravel to MD for quarterly planning, if not local.

Benefits

Comprehensive benefit package thatincludes 3 weeks paid time off, 10+ Paid Holidays, medical/dental coverage, STD,LTD, Life Insurance, AD&D, 401k with up to 4% match, and end of year profitsharing.

jobs.description:
About the Role

Join a paid talent pool supporting projects in AI agents and reinforcement learning. You will help build practice environments and evaluate agent behavior, supporting the development of AI systems that interact with software and workflows.

What You'll Do

  • Build reinforcement learning environments in Python and Docker where agents can take actions and receive feedback.

  • Turn business workflows, such as ERP processes, CRM updates, and spreadsheet operations, into trainable scenarios.

  • Write tasks, connect tools and REST APIs, and create systems to verify agent actions.

  • Create and grade agent demonstrations, including screen recordings of task execution.

  • Collect execution traces, evaluate agent trajectories, and investigate failures.

What We're Looking For

  • Zero to five years of experience in software engineering, QA automation, machine learning or reinforcement learning engineering, operations analysis, or substantial use of business software.

  • Experience writing Python or building automations or reports in Excel, Salesforce, or an ERP system.

  • Experience testing, scripting, or automating multi-step software tasks, such as test cases, API calls, or UI steps.

  • Familiarity with Docker, REST APIs, or Gymnasium and OpenAI Gym-style environments is useful.

  • Experience with pytest, Playwright, or Selenium, or documenting business workflows and screen-based tasks, is useful.

  • Strong software fundamentals or hands-on knowledge of business workflows; prior AI data experience is not required.

Compensation & Benefits

Compensation is $35 to $70 per hour, depending on the project, field, and experience. Payment is based on hours worked.

Location

Remote. Projects typically last from one week to several months.

Compensation Range: $72.8K - $145.6K
